clauses.reason: Section 1 establishes the Humanitarian Service Medal, to be awarded by the Secretary of Defense or the Secretary of Transportation for the Coast Guard (when not in the Navy) to members of the armed forces who meritoriously participated after April 1, 1975 in a humanitarian military act or operation. EO 13286 sec. 55 substituted the Secretary of Homeland Security for the Secretary of Transportation (effective March 1, 2003); the clause continues amended and the Code note prints it that way.

research_rationale:
Identity: Executive Order 11965 of January 19, 1977, 42 FR 4329 (Jan. 24, 1977), held at jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11965.txt (FR Doc. 77-2397); it establishes the Humanitarian Service Medal (secs. 1-4: establishment and eligibility, design and precedence, one medal with devices, posthumous award). The preamble recites authority as President and Commander in Chief and cites no statute. Later instrument: EO 13286 sec. 55 (signed Feb. 28, 2003; effective March 1, 2003 under its sec. 92) struck the Secretary of Transportation wherever it appears in sections 1, 2 and 4 and inserted the Secretary of Homeland Security (OFR note: amended by EO 13286). Section 3 is untouched. Searches of held texts find only EO 13286, the 1989 OFR codification line and the 6 U.S.C. 111 note. The Code note prints the amended order. Bounded searches read for coverage: current-law:usc (U.S. Code release point 119-121 USLM text and notes, citations of the order by number, edition current through 2026-10-09, laws enacted 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-14 not reflected), current-law:ecfr (eCFR point-in-time search as of 2026-10-14 plus GovInfo CFR bulk XML, 49 titles) and later-events:ofr_catalog (Office of the Federal Register disposition notes of 6941 catalog records plus operative sentences in 17521 saved order texts).
